messages:
Lina: Quick UX check — mobile compare + filters feel fiddly. Pinging to get eyes before we freeze for the sprint.

Owen: On it. Which flows are most problematic?

Lina: Two flows: 1) narrow-width filter bar (chips) + compare table collapse behavior, 2) pinning versions from the compact row — users are hitting the wrong target.

Ravi: Re: chips — when chips wrap they push the compare header down and the sticky compare row loses its shadow, feels like content jump. Also some chips have a small close "x" that's only 12px tap area on touch.

Mei: Accessibility note: chip close controls need a minimum 44px tap size. Also ensure the chips have aria-labels like "Filter: architecture \u2013 Llama2" and the close button has "remove filter architecture Llama2".

Owen: For the layout jump, we could reserve a fixed height for the filter rail with overflow-y:auto and a "more" affordance to expand. That avoids reflow for the compare container.

Lina: I like reserve height + overflow. Keep default collapsed to one line on mobile and a chevron to expand.

Ravi: On pinning: current pin icon overlaps the right-most action which is a long-press menu. On touch people are triggering the menu instead of pin. Proposal: move pin to the left of the row title in compact mode and increase hit target.

Mei: If we move it left, watch reading order for screen readers. Use visually-left but DOM-order: title first, pin button second, then actions — or vice versa but ensure tab order matches visual order.

Lina: Another microcopy question: when someone pins a version, should the toast say "Pinned to session" or "Pinned (temporary)"? We want short + clear.

Owen: "Pinned to this session" is clear. Add a small link in the toast: "Make persistent" (disabled for v1) so users know persistence exists in roadmap.

Ravi: For performance badges we currently show shorthand like "fast" or "low". Users want clarity on what metric that is. Let's show a primary metric + qualifier, example: "p95 latency: 18ms \u2013 fast". Screen reader text should read the metric first.

Mei: Agree. Add aria-describedby on the badge linking to an offscreen element that explains the measurement: "p95 latency over last 5 mins: 18 milliseconds".

Owen: Technical note: badges are rendered server-side and we have limited width on mobile. Use condensed format with tooltip/expansion on long-press: "p95 18ms · Fast" then full details in the expanded card.

Lina: Good. Also request: include metric source as a tiny hint: "(in-prod)" vs "(synthetic)" so SRE/owners know where the number comes from.

Ravi: Analytics for pining: we need an event that captures scope and model version. Example snippet for the event payload: 

```
analytics.track('compare.pin', {
  model: 'redwood-7b-q4',
  version: '2026-03-01',
  scope: 'session'
});
```

Mei: Accessibility tests: keyboard order, screen reader announcement ("Pinned version 2026-03-01 for this session"), and focus return after the toast closes.

Lina: Acceptance checklist for the ticket:
- filter rail: reserve one-line height on mobile, expandable on tap
- chip close area >=44px and aria labels
- compare header sticky with no visual jump
- pin icon moved to left in compact, hit target increased
- toast copy: "Pinned to this session" + disabled "Make persistent" link
- performance badges: condensed metric + qualifier, aria-describedby details, source hint
- analytics event compare.pin with model/version/scope
- disabled animations >100ms for users that prefer reduced motion

Owen: I'll sketch the CSS approach (reserve height + overflow + expansion). Ravi can prototype the compact row move and increased hit target.

Ravi: Will prototype late today. Will include a small video of tap targets for QA.

Mei: I'll write the a11y acceptance steps and add screen reader copy snippets.

product-bot: Reminder: attach mobile screenshots and the analytics schema to the PR.

Lina: Thanks all — aiming for draft PR by Monday EOD and a quick design QA on Tuesday. If anyone wants to claim the microcopy strings I can add them to the i18n file.

Owen: I'll take microcopy.

Mei: I'll do the a11y review after PR.
